acceptance_gate: A runs a frozen exploratory census with an independent check; B proves the counterexamples and the positive constructions it states; every census case agrees with the predictions or the disagreement is reported.
objective: Serves open question 3 of docs/KNOT_INTUITION.md (composition) after MALTSEV-CONVERSE-20261020-001, which reduced the converse of the difference-law theorem to a local converse (in a law whose knots compose like cycles, every knot is rectangular) and recommended the diagonal lemma: every non-rectangular 3-variable knot with neither a meeting variable nor a selector has a diagonal derivation exists h: K(x0, x0, h) and K(x1, x2, h) that has one. Scoping on 2026-10-21 found that the lemma and the local converse both fail: the product of a difference law whose systems all have full ranges with a non-rectangular factor that it dominates (a shadow) has the difference law's constrained sets in every system. A (exploratory census) maps where the lemma holds: random 3-variable knots on 3 to 6 values (direct cases, a fibre-distance construction, the diagonal derivation, and systems without cross-position identification), random 4-variable knots, group-action knots, random shadows, and small domains for counterexamples. B proves the shadow theorem with counterexamples on 6 values (3 variables) and 4 values (4 variables), proves the fibre-distance construction, and states what composing knots like cycles still forces.
status: Complete 2026-10-21. The diagonal lemma and the local converse are false: K4 = (x+y+z=0 mod 3 on {0,1,2,3}, reading 3 as 2) minus (2,2,2) is a non-rectangular 3-variable knot with no direct case whose law composes all circuits like cycles, because in every system it has the constrained sets of x+y+z=0 over Z3 (lift theorem); products with a dominating difference law do the same (shadow theorem). Composition sees only which sets are constrained; it still forces no direct case and disconnected or dense fibre graphs (fibre-distance construction). The lemma holds for every random knot tested; two values admit no counterexample, three are open. Census A (refuted on candidates, all resolved), proof B (proved), ledger Z. Recommendation: Continue with the matroid-level converse (2/3), deferred to the owner.
stop_rule: Stop after B. Stop earlier if a shadow system shows a failure between circuits, which would reopen the local converse.
title: The diagonal lemma: does composing knots like cycles force rectangular knots?
